Tulane University

Mahir Bilen Can

I am a professor of mathematics at Tulane University. My research focuses on algebraic groups and monoids, representation theory, algebraic geometry, and applications to coding theory and secure communication.

Office
Gibson Hall, Room 319, New Orleans, LA
Research
Algebraic groups, representation theory, algebraic geometry, coding theory

Education

  • University of Pennsylvania PhD (2006)
  • METU (Turkey) BSc (2001)

Research

Themes

Research page

  • Algebraic groups and monoids

    Structure, classification, and geometric properties, with applications to representation theory and combinatorics.

  • Representation theory

    Interactions between representations, geometry, and number theory, especially where symmetry clarifies complex systems.

  • Algebraic geometry

    Geometric methods for understanding algebraic structures and moduli, connecting geometry with computational techniques.

  • Error-correcting codes and secure communication

    Algebraic and geometric approaches to robust communication, coding theory, and cryptographic protocols.
